title: Lesson 22 - When Declarative Runs Out: Apex, LWC, AppExchange, and Productivity Tools
description: Given a scenario, determine when it's appropriate to extend declarative development with custom development, third-party applications, Salesforce products, or productivity tools (email integrations, Slack, Salesforce Mobile).

questions.question: You must process five hundred thousand records nightly with complex amount recalculation and tight governor-limit control. What do you build?
options: A screen Flow launched from a list button
A batch Apex class scheduled nightly
A validation rule with a formula
questions.explanation: Large-volume nightly processing with complex logic and governor-limit control is a named Apex boundary that a Flow's limits cannot meet.

questions.question: A managed package installed in your org is consuming your CPU governor limits. What is true?
options: Managed package Apex runs in an isolated limits context
Apex in managed packages still counts against your org's governor limits
You can edit the package's Apex to reduce its consumption
Governor limits apply only to your own Apex
questions.explanation: Packaged Apex executes inside your org against your limits, and because package components are locked you cannot edit it to reduce consumption.

questions.question: Which email integration syncs email and events into a separate activity store rather than as reportable EmailMessage records?
questions.explanation: Einstein Activity Capture syncs Gmail and Outlook email and events into a separate activity store, which is why those activities are not fully reportable as EmailMessage records.
